name: Mibsar
title: Edomite tribal chief
summary: Mibsar was one of the tribal chiefs (alufim) who descended from Esau, Jacob's twin brother. He is mentioned in the genealogies of Edom and represents one of the Edomite clans that settled in the mountains of Seir. The name Mibsar may mean 'fortress' or 'fortified place,' which could suggest a connection to a fortified city in Edom.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned among the tribal chiefs of Edom in Genesis
keyEvents.description: Mibsar is listed as one of the tribal chiefs descended from Esau in the land of Edom, in the genealogy that concludes the account of Esau's descendants.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the genealogy of Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Mibsar is again listed among the tribal chiefs of Edom in the great genealogy of 1 Chronicles, confirming his place in Edomite history.

keyEvents.title: Esau's lineage in Edom
keyEvents.description: Mibsar belongs to the broader narrative of Esau's descendants who formed the Edomite people, a neighboring nation to Israel with a long and complex history.

keyEvents.title: Kings and chiefs of Edom
keyEvents.description: Before Israel had kings, Edom already had an organized tribal system with chiefs and kings, of which Mibsar was part of this leadership.
